previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a four-day history of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, during which she stopped her insulin therapy, leading to severe hyperglycemia and mild diabetic ketoacidosis. IV insulin rapidly corrected her anion gap, and her symptoms improved with supportive care. She was restarted on her home regimen of 60 units of Lantus at bedtime and her usual Humalog sliding scale, with continuation of oral hydromorphone for pain and omeprazole for gastric protection. Her condition stabilized within hours, and after coordination with her primary care provider, she was discharged home with instructions to follow up in two days. No medication changes were made, and she demonstrated understanding of her insulin management. The port in her chest was de-accessed due to poor function and will require outpatient evaluation.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms ___ is a ___ yo female with type 1 diabetes, complicated by 
gastroparesis, with frequent rehospitalizations for abdominal 
pain and nausea, who presents with six days of nausea, vomiting, 
abdominal pain and inability to tolerate PO for three days, 
similar to prior hospitalizations. 

Patient received IV fluids and medications as per the defined 
protocol for these complaints in OMR note dated ___. 
Overnight, patient became angry with staff for using the GJ tube 
for medications and therefore pulled out her own GJ tube. Under 
consultation with her PCP and psychiatric services, it was 
decided not to replace it. Patient left with desire to have it 
replaced at another hospital.
Before leaving, patient also expressed desire to kill or hurt 
someone, specifically an older male roommate who has been 
sexually assaulting her. She then said she would not go home and 
that she has places to go. She spoke to a psychiatric nurse 
before leaving the hospital.

# Nausea/Vomiting/Abdominal Pain: DDx includes flare of chronic 
pancreatitis given radiation to back though lipase wnl vs 
gastroparesis in the setting of poor glycemic control. Pt. has 
had extensive workup in the past for abdominal pain and no 
further diagnostic studies seem necessary at this time.
-Hydromorphone 0.5-1mg IV Q3H:PRN pain and then PO per protocol
-Tolerated a sandwich and crackers overnight - caused pain but 
no more nausea or vomiting

# Diabetes: sugars critically high in ED (527), then 228 after 
10 units of Humalog. No ketones in urine. She received 80% of 
her home dose while she wasn't eating. Glucose 414 again this 
morning. Returned home on home dose of diabetes medications and 
a diabetic diet.

# Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis: AG 15 in ED with no ketones in 
urine with resolution by the morning of discharge. DKA vs 
starvation ketoacidosis vs lactic acidosis. Lactate of 2.5 but 
no acidosis this morning.
  
# SI/HI
Overnight, patient reported SI if she did not receive pain meds 
but that she would not be suicidal if she receives pain meds 
with no plan. This morning, endorsed HI for someone at home, at 
times not specifying and at other times referring to her 
roommate. On the floor, she was accompanied by security. H/o 
borderline PD and previous suicide attempts/cutting.  
  
# Hyponatremia
Na 132 on arrival, likely due to SIADH or possibly from vomiting 
137 on discharge, euvolemic on exam, taking PO.

# Asthma
Stable, no wheeze on exam, normal O2 sats. Continue home 
medications.

# Chronic Pain
Pt. on PO hydromorphone and gabapentin as outpatient.  

# Anxiety
Continue home diazepam, diphenhydramine, trazodone, mirtazapine
